region: Industry City, Sunset Park · Brooklyn, New York
about: Fort Hamilton Distillery was founded in 2016 by Alex Clark, a British-born bartender who spent years in New York’s classic-cocktail scene, and his wife, Amy Grindeland. Their mission was to bring back New York’s earliest whiskey style, rye, and the distillery takes its name from Fort Hamilton at the southern tip of Brooklyn, itself named for Alexander Hamilton. Since 2020 the company has had its own distillery and tasting room on the second floor of a converted warehouse in Industry City, on the Sunset Park waterfront.

Double Barrel is Fort Hamilton’s blended bourbon, built for mixing as much as sipping. It marries two straight bourbons: a New York bourbon distilled at Taconic Distillery in Stanfordville from 100% New York-grown grain (70% corn, 25% rye, 5% malted barley) and a high-rye bourbon from MGP in Lawrenceburg, Indiana (60% corn, 36% rye, 4% malted barley). Both are aged in 53-gallon barrels at a number 3 char, then blended, bottled at 92 proof and never chill filtered.

The distillery describes aromas of cacao, cardamom, turmeric and apricot-studded chocolate, with green peppercorn, caramel corn and orange zest on the palate. Wine Enthusiast’s reviewer found that a splash of water brings out cinnamon and ginger before a maple-tinged finish. The generous rye content is deliberate: Clark, who spent his career behind the bar, designed it to stand up in an Old Fashioned or a Manhattan.
